questions.prompt: The spot price of oil stays at $80. Each month you buy the next contract at $82 and hold it to expiry. What happens to your money each month?
options: It stays the same, because the oil price did not move
questions.explanation: At expiry the contract is worth the spot price, $80. The growth factor is 80 / 82 = 0.9756, a loss of 2.44% each month.

questions.prompt: The futures curve for oil falls: contracts with later expiries cost less. What is this shape called, and what does it do to a rolled long position?
options: Backwardation, and it adds return as each contract rises to the spot price
Contango, and it subtracts return as each contract falls to the spot price
Backwardation, and it subtracts return as each contract falls to the spot price
Contango, and it adds return as each contract rises to the spot price
questions.explanation: A falling curve is backwardation. You buy the next contract below the spot price, and it rises to the spot price by expiry, so each roll gains.

questions.prompt: Why does a rolled long position lose money in contango even when the spot price never moves?
options: Because the exchange charges a fee at each roll
Because each contract is bought above the spot price and falls to it by expiry
Because the spot price is always above the futures price
questions.explanation: In contango the next contract costs more than the spot price. At expiry it is worth the spot price, so the holder loses the gap at every roll.
